title: Polynomial equations with a unit Jacobian minor near a regular closed point
statement: Let k be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure], S a finite type k-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], and m a maximal ideal such that S_m is regular local [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime, def-weil-regular-scheme]. There exist g in S outside m, natural numbers n,c, polynomials f_j in k[y_1,...,y_n] indexed by j in Fin c [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], a k-algebra isomorphism e: k[y_1,...,y_n]/(f_j) -> S_g [def-weil-ring-localization-away], and a strictly increasing map i: Fin c -> Fin n, such that the quotient image of det(partial f_j/partial y_(i(l)))_(j,l) is a unit [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant, def-weil-pbc-polynomial-partial-derivative]. This asserts a specified algebraic presentation and an invertible minor; smoothness is not a premise or conclusion.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00TS, implication (1) => (4), polynomial-presentation and conormal-rank argument; Lemma 00TE, converse inverse-variable construction

proof.text: Take a finite polynomial presentation phi:P -> S, where P=k[X_1,...,X_N], with kernel I, and let M=phi^{-1}(m). The ideal M is maximal. The polynomial localization A=P_M is regular local; A/IA is isomorphic to S_m, regular by hypothesis. The proved independent-generators theorem supplies a finite set generating IA whose cotangent classes in A are independent.

Write each chosen generator of IA as f_j/s_j with f_j in I and s_j outside M. Multiplication by the nonzero residue of s_j preserves independence, so the classes of f_j are independent. The closed-point cotangent comparison identifies dim cotangent(A) with the polynomial differential fibre dimension. The canonical conormal map to this fibre is surjective by the conormal exact sequence and Omega_{kappa(M)/k}=0; equal finite dimensions make it an isomorphism. In the polynomial differential basis, the images of f_j are their gradient vectors. Independence therefore gives a nonzero square minor Delta; its image phi(Delta) is outside m.

source.place: Lemma 00TS, independent linear terms and final Jacobian rank argument; Lemma 00TR

proof.text: Set J=(f_j). The finite P-module I/J has zero localization at M because JA=IA. Choose finite generators of I/J. For each generator the zero-fraction criterion gives an element outside M annihilating it. Their finite product b is outside M and annihilates all of I/J. Thus (I/J)_b=0 and P_b/JP_b -> S_{phi(b)} is an isomorphism.

source.place: Lemma 00TS, finitely generated kernel vanishing after localization

proof.text: Let g=phi(b)*phi(Delta), outside m. Adjoin variables z,w and equations bz-1, Delta*w-1 to P/J. The quotient is isomorphic to S_g by the universal properties of polynomial algebras, quotients and localization. Select the old minor variables together with z,w. The enlarged Jacobian block is triangular with determinant b*Delta^2, a unit because both b and Delta have explicit inverses in the quotient. Reorder the selected variables increasingly, changing the determinant at most by a unit sign. Empty equation sets use Delta=1, and a zero I/J uses b=1. The map to S_g sends X_i to phi(X_i), z to phi(b) inverse and w to phi(Delta) inverse. For the inverse, I maps to zero because b annihilates I/J and is invertible; descend P to S and extend to S_g using invertibility of g. The composites fix these polynomial generators and their specified inverses, so are identities.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_jacobian_unit_presentation_of_regularAtMaximal
    (k : Type u) (S : Type v) [Field k] [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
    [IsAlgClosed k] [Algebra.FiniteType k S]
    (m : Ideal S) (hm : m.IsMaximal)
    (hreg : IsRegularLocalRing (Localization.AtPrime m)) :
    ∃ (g : S), g ∉ m ∧
      ∃ (n c : ℕ) (f : Fin c → MvPolynomial (Fin n) k)
        (e : (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range f)) ≃ₐ[k]
          Localization.Away g) (i : Fin c → Fin n),
        StrictMono i ∧ IsUnit (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span (Set.range f))
          (Matrix.det (fun j l : Fin c ↦ MvPolynomial.pderiv (i l) (f j))))
